CursorEpic Arch · 16%
Risk Pure debut with no exposed ability over 8f on AW.
AP O'Brien stable pecking order among three runnerslive market/late scratchingsopening pace map with possible pacemaker
Epic Arch gets the nod mainly on race shape, not price: draw 1 in a 13-runner Dundalk mile is a material edge on this card, and Andrew Slattery’s yard is the hottest local connection here (3 wins from 22 in the last fortnight, strong 6-month rank). Booking himself on a debut from the inside stall fits a purposeful ride rather than a field-filler, and at equal weights with the rest this is one of the few spots where geography and trainer intent outweigh the blank formbook.

The biggest threat is Moliere, who brings the only solid recent form — fourth at Galway over 7f, beaten only 0.8L on yielding ground 19 days ago from draw 4, a profile that often translates to an AW mile second time out. The main worry for Epic Arch is that debutants can still run green or find 8f too much first time; if Slattery’s colt lacks tactical speed or stamina, Moliere’s proven competitiveness beats a draw-led hunch.

CursorMount Atlas · 28%
Risk Dubai Honour carries the top OR off a Haggas layoff and could outclass this field if fully fit.
pace map and likely lead horsefirmness shift from York GF prepDubai Honour turf-fitness evidence after 126 days idle
Mount Atlas is the form anchor: he won York’s 14f Good To Firm Class 1 trial from Tabletalk (0.2L), with prior 14f placings at Chester and Musselburgh, strong Good-ground figures (2-4), and Andrew Balding’s yard in sharp order. Tabletalk is the obvious danger on the same form line and trip suitability (1-4 at distance), but Mount Atlas has already proven superiority over him. Dubai Honour tops the ratings and justifies market respect, yet his recent profile is overwhelmingly AW, he has no course/distance evidence here, and 126 days off makes his 2.6 price a talent bet rather than a proven one — I would not treat that short quote as proof of winning chance today.

The main risk to Mount Atlas is Dubai Honour translating superior class to turf at 13.5f if Haggas has him ready first time back; a strong pace could also compress margins and favour the highest-rated stayer. Gamrai is an improver but faces a steep Class 1 rise on figures, while Wine Dark Sea and Rebel Rocker look outclassed on ratings and recent Group-level form.

CursorChristian David · 20%
Risk Hannon also runs fresh Thirsk winner Witch Hunter, so tactics and split stable intent could blunt the obvious setup.
confirmed pace map / possible pacemaker roletoday's firmness vs his 0-4 good-going win recordWitch Hunter Thirsk-to-Class-2 class jump
Christian David is the structural play rather than the market leader. He is the lightest-weight effective runner in a tight handicap, brings proven Newbury seven-furlong form (1-3 course-and-distance), and lands on draw 8 where this track’s six-year sample strongly favours high stalls (44% of winners). Recent runs stack up well for this test: close fifth in a Class 2 at Ascot and fourth over seven furlongs on good ground at Doncaster, with three career wins at the trip. Scoville’s favouritism looks price-driven; his figures are patchy, he is 0-2 at seven furlongs and 0-0 here, and draw six sits in the weaker middle band.

The main danger is not Addison Grey’s seven-furlong query alone but the Richard Hannon double. Witch Hunter’s crisp Thirsk win seven days ago brings momentum and a five-pound claim, and stablemates can reshape the race even when the obvious candidate has the best draw-and-weight profile. If the pace collapses late from the stands side, Addison Grey (draw seven, repeatedly beaten only a neck or less lately) is the most likely beneficiary behind Christian David.

Andrew Balding’s yard is the strongest trainer signal on this card (#3 nationally on six-month wins), and in a Class 2 maiden that matters more than the market’s clustering at the top of the odds list. Silent Force gets a workable middle draw (28% band—not ideal on the 7f high-draw bias, but not a low-stall penalty either), and P J McDonald is a solid, experienced booking for a first-time-out horse at this level.

San Jose is the main rival: Tom Marquand is in strong recent form, stall 12 sits in the favoured high third (44% of winners), and Brian Meehan’s yard has been winning lately. Lots Road (draw 13, Beckett/Crouch) and the form runners—Red Tail’s sharp 6f debut and Another Encore’s close 7f Class 2 run at Ascot—are each plausible but carry clearer negatives (trip/draw for Red Tail; big-price profile and wide draw execution for Another Encore). I would not treat the short-looking prices on several unraced horses as proof of ability; at ~12% true win chance, Silent Force is a marginal play rather than a strong conviction bet in a wide-open field.

Masterinthewoods looks the most fairly weighted winner on draw and form. Stall 6 fits Newbury 12f bias (high draws ~41% of winners); the profile is progressive and reliable — second at Ascot over 12f on Good To Firm and second at Goodwood over 12f on Good — without needing the top weight. Marco Ghiani is a solid booking and the horse is only 6lb below Great Bedwyn on OR, with better recent consistency than the favourite on paper.

The main doubt is the bare 0-2 Good To Firm win record, even though he has run well on fast ground elsewhere; Explode is the closest danger on a proven 12f Good To Firm win (Catterick), perfect going stats (1-1), and William Buick, offset by a less favourable draw and a colder yard. Great Bedwyn has top weight, Newbury CD form (1-2), and Richard Hannon, but Thirsk stewards’ “never travelling” and patchy 628283 form cap him below the front two; Tryfan’s Ascot win is offset by draw 2 against bias, a possible pacemaker role, and Callum Rodriguez’s 0-11 J14; Nicator and debut Pinatique (draw 1, no form) sit below the main contenders.

actual market odds (all listed at 1.1)pace map and whether Wild Thoughts is committed up frontcurrent handicap marks after July wins
Golden Knight is the most convincing fit on today's terms: he has already won at 10f on Good To Firm, carries a workable mark from that Ascot success, and gets a mid draw in a race where the last six years at Newbury around this trip slightly favour the middle stalls. Ed Walker and Hector Crouch are both riding well, and he arrives with fresher, more trip-specific evidence than most rivals. Dream Camp is the main danger on weight — 9st 0lb off OR 82, with Andrew Balding and Rob Hornby in strong form and a recent Windsor 10f Good To Firm win — while Lost Signal's draw-one slot and Good-ground record are positives, but he is still a stamina query first time at a mile and a quarter.

The biggest risk to Golden Knight is that his case rests heavily on one narrow-field Ascot win; Bayaann's superior rating is undermined by the same course-and-trip flop, but Dream Camp's lighter weight and Lost Signal's low draw could both overturn him if the race develops tactically against a horse that has not yet proven himself in a truly competitive 10f handicap. I would not treat any short price here as proof of ability — this looks a genuine six-way puzzle with no runner much above a one-in-four…

Al Qayed gets the narrow edge on the most concrete course factor in the brief: at Newmarket (July) over 8f, high draws have supplied 46% of winners versus 16% from low — a meaningful swing in a three-runner field where he holds the outside. That pairs with William Haggas (#6 trainer on this card), a yard that routinely has debutants ready for this sort of Class 3 task, and Cieren Fallon in respectable recent form (6-24 J14, #6 jockey). Waaqed looks the weakest package on paper — low-draw bias headwind plus Robert Havlin’s cooler six-month and 14-day numbers (#45, 2-13 J14) — leaving roughly a third of the win pool for him.

The main threat is Bin Jahwar: Billy Loughnane is the stand-out jockey on the card (#1, 121-595) and Charlie Appleby’s yard is the hottest of the three recently (6-10 T14). His middle draw (39% winner band) is still fair, and on debut races where breeding and preparation are hidden, that jockey-and-yard heat can easily beat a draw-led call — which is why confidence stays modest and the model’s no-qualifier stance is reasonable.

The Doncaster win was the right trip and surface; OR 70 in a six-runner C3 handicap looks fair rather than flattered, and draw 4 is workable. Dojin is next best on bare ability (OR 83) and has run over this exact C&D (2nd here in June), with Fallon riding well, but that July defeat was seven lengths adrift and he is 0-2 on good ground — form that fits the trip less cleanly than Reem Rak's.

The main worry is freshness and class: fifty days off and a step from C5 to C3 mean the Doncaster display must be repeated, and the Ffos Las stewards' note (hung/interference when second) flags a temperament risk over this long July bend. If Alma Latina settles better over 14f than her Sandown flop, her 9-0 and Billy Loughnane could outrun this estimate; I still prefer the proven stayer with the weight edge.

O'Leary yard tactics with two runnersprecise pace map / potential pacemakerFemme Beauty Irish form on Good
Del Corso is the logical winner on substance, not price. Back-to-back 10f wins on Good To Firm at Nottingham, top OR (67), proven on today's ground (2-3), and the strongest trainer-jockey pair on the card (Loughnane #1, Walker in form). The Lingfield stewards' note that he wanted a quicker surface is a positive today, not a negative. He is clearly ahead of Dont Get Me Wrong on ratings and recent form, and well ahead of Femme Beauty on suitability — she is 0-0 on Good and arrives off Irish Yield form with a cold trainer record (T14 0-0).

I would not treat 1.1 or the model's 63% as fair — four-runner handicaps are volatile, and the draw profile hurts Del Corso (stall 2; high draws win ~48% here). Pipily is the main danger: second by a short head over this course and distance in July on the same going, with course experience Kent's yard lacks elsewhere. Femme Beauty gets a draw boost from stall 4 but needs a big step up on ground and from Irish company; my true win estimate (~46%) is well below market-implied dominance but still makes Del Corso the pick over Pipily (~27%).

Biggles is the most credible winner on the evidence that matters for a Good-ground 16f Class 4 hurdle. OR 102 sits near the top of the handicap, he is fit off 22 days, and his latest run is almost a direct read-through: fifth at Uttoxeter over 16f on good ground in the same class, beaten only 1L with no P/F/U in the form string. That beats short-price reputation and puts him ahead of Crackalackin, whose 2nd at Huntingdon is the main rival profile but is stale after 88 days and still without a win on good or at this trip. Hawthorn Road’s close Perth run and hot Iain Jardine yard earn respect, but three career starts, a prior pull-up, and unknown rating cap him below the top two. Try Them’s OR 109 is offset by a recent fall and thin experience; St Just In Time’s last two AW flat runs are poor hurdle prep.

The biggest risk to Biggles is that he has not converted similar opportunities: 0-2 over today’s distance and a trainer/jockey combo going 0-0 in the last 14 days. In a seven-runner handicap where several have plausible excuses, his true chance is only about one win in four—not the certainty the 1.1 quotes imply—so the edge is form/trip/fitness alignment rather than dominance.

Tamarind Bay is the most plausible winner on the card: top OR (123), proven over 20f on good ground, clean recent jumping (no P/F/U), and Sean Bowen — the strongest jockey here by a wide margin on six-month NH numbers. The Uttoxeter win 48 days ago is the best direct form line for this trip, class, and going, and his Doncaster/Newcastle runs confirm he stays. I have him at roughly 41%, not 51%; in a five-runner handicap that is a clear edge on ability but far from a lock.

The main danger is Ras Kassar (~27%): David Pipe, 20 days since a 1.2L second over 20f good at Uttoxeter, lighter in the weights, and jumping has held so far on his sole chase start. Follow Your Luck is hard to dismiss entirely on two wins at around 20f, but 177 days off into a Class 3 handicap chase with unknown OR and only C4 form caps him near 10%. Kinbara Firstdraft has Perth course runs but declining form (7th over 16f here last time); Glen To Glen is outclassed on OR and profile for this grade.

Dalileo is the most race-fit profile on the card: he won at Perth three weeks ago, carries a workable 11-10 off OR 90, and his Perth record (3-16, 2-13 CD) is the strongest course evidence in the field. He has completed over this trip here (third in a Perth 24f handicap in June on Good) and his jumping has been reliable lately — no P/F/U in his last six starts — which matters more than the higher-rated but erratic Ceol Draiochta or the top-weight Dolly Dior, whose Perth form (fourth beaten 42L, seventh) undercuts the Hexham win.

The main reservation is that June third was a long way behind, so he may need the race to collapse rather than dominate on pure stamina; Drumlee Myth (recent 22f Good winner, light weight) and October Hill (consistent frames, though 0-8 on Good winners) are the likeliest to beat him if the extra two furlongs find him out. I would not treat any runner as a strong betting proposition — true win chance tops out around one-in-five in an open eleven-runner handicap — which aligns with the model passing the race.

Scriabin is the runner whose form maps most cleanly onto today: three straight placed efforts at Perth over 16f on good ground, most recently second of twelve beaten only 0.2L in June. That is stronger local evidence than anything else in the field brings. At OR 103 he carries roughly 21lb less than topweight The Last Cloud, which matters in an eight-runner handicap, and his recent jumping has been reliable — no P/F/U in the current spell — with a respectable 44-day refresh and Lucinda Russell’s yard in reasonable heart by the card ranks.

The main danger is that those Perth runs were Class 4, whereas this is Class 2, so the 0.2L near-miss may not translate once Filibustering and Squeezebox bring fresher Class 2 form — Filibustering won over hurdles at Cartmel last time and Squeezebox was third in a similar 16f Good C2 at Market Rasen. I would not stake The Last Cloud at anything like a 46% true win chance: 168 days off, pulled up last start, and cold T14/J14 figures outweigh the CD 3-3 and top OR; Medieval Gold’s course win is also stale at 172 days. Pure Gold’s recent fall and Perth disappointments leave him as the likeliest outsider.

Edgewell is the most trustworthy chaser here on the factors you listed: he has completed his last three starts with two Class 4/5 chase wins on Good (Worcester 23f, Newton Abbot 26f), giving him the best trip-and-fitness profile for 24f today. His 5-18 on Good and 3-7 at around this distance outweigh the higher official marks on others; Shantou Show and Collingham bring recent PUs into a fence race, Ballydangan is off 149 days and pulled up last time, and Button Rock looks short of chase form. Mcgregors Charge is the main danger on Perth course form (1-1, CD 1-1) and a useful 10-7 claim from OR 82, but he was only fourth at Newton Abbot beaten 5L — behind the winner Edgewell’s stablemate form line — and his jumping is still patchy (PP earlier in the string).

The biggest risk to Edgewell is course naivety at Perth combined with the Warwick steward’s note that he was pulled up when never travelling; that keeps his true win chance closer to 28% than favourite certainty in a seven-runner handicap where Le Malin (high OR but amateur rider, small-field Cartmel third) and Bowen on the unreliable-jumping Shantou Show can still land a share. I would not treat this as a strong staking race…

CursorNO BET · 27%
Risk Coral Cove is unproven at 8f and the 1.5 price overstates her chance in a wide-open Class 2.
pace map with three Easterby runnersdebutant homework/workOR marks all missing
On form and connections, Coral Cove is the clearest winner candidate: she beat Rule Of The Agency, Special Operations and The First Drop when winning at York over 7f on good ground, James Owen and Jason Hart are among the hottest yard/rider combos on the card, and draw 12 fits Ripon’s high-draw 8f bias (45% of winners). Temple Court is next best on profile — four runs, prior Class 2 exposure, progressive placings and a useful high draw — but she is still searching for a win and is stepping up in trip.

I would not stake the race because the market has Coral Cove at 1.5 (~67% implied) while a fair read — extra furlong, several debutants from capable yards (including Tudhope on Dee’s Mochafella from a strong stall), and no model support — caps her true chance nearer 27%. That gap, plus the usual variance from lightly raced rivals, makes this a pass despite a logical favourite on paper.

CursorRogue Jewel · 30%
Risk Draw 2 fights Ripon’s high-draw 6f bias and four rivals are shorter in the market despite none having won.
Taj Mahal Palace debut/trial strengthearly pace and run-style mapofficial ratings all unknown
Rogue Jewel is the only runner with a win, and it was over today’s six furlongs on good ground at York in a competitive field, with a 1lb weight edge and Daniel Tudhope in strong recent form for Edward Bethell — that is a clearer ability signal than any rival’s form. Green Bay Dream has Ripon experience but was well beaten here and is on the wrong side of the draw; Classy Jaguar’s Beverley flop (shoe lost) and cold Nolan booking are hard to forgive; Taj Mahal Palace gets the best draw but is an unknown debut.

The main doubt is setup, not talent: Ripon’s six-furlong stats favour high draws, and Does Mary Know (draw 4) already has Class 2 six-furlong experience on good ground at Goodwood, so she is the likeliest danger if Rogue Jewel does not translate its York win into a front-running or stalking trip from a low draw. I would not stake this at a 58% win chance — in a five-runner Class 2 juvenile, 30% is a fair true estimate versus the market’s clustered short prices.

CursorMagic Boy · 11%
Risk Apprentice jockey in a hot 20-runner sprint where high draws are strongly favoured but he is not the only one drawn well.
Exact pace map with four Tim Easterby runnersWhether Ripon rides genuinely Good or fasterMythical Composer price/role if 1.1 is a feed error vs a declared pacemaker
Magic Boy looks the most plausible winner on merit, not price. He won a deep 19-runner York six-furlong handicap on good to firm in July, was beaten only a neck there next time, and maps well to today: same trip, similar class, good ground, and draw 14 which fits Ripon's high-draw edge (43% of winners). Ripon form from June (close second) adds course suitability. Grant Wood is the main danger: he ran fourth over course and distance here 12 days ago off a higher mark and has strong CD figures (1-6), with Jason Hart in good form, but his mid draw is a meaningful negative in this field size and he was well behind Magic Boy on the same York form reference.

The biggest risk is that this is still only an ~11% true win chance in a 20-runner sprint — no runner dominates. Glory Hyde (CD 2-2, draw 19), Mark's Choice (prolific Ripon form, draw 17, light weight), and the well-handicapped Educating Rita all have live claims if the race develops wrong for Magic Boy, and the Easterby quartet adds tactical uncertainty around pace and which horse gets the best trip.

live pace map / early speedexact Good-to-Firm vs Good split on Ripon 6f todayEasterby/Walford multi-runner stable tactics
This is a genuinely open Class 2 fifteen-runner sprint where no runner clears my bar for a staking edge. On true ability I lean **Dark Cloud Rising** (~11%) ahead of **Lord Roxby** (~10%): the higher OR, Ripon C2 course win, high-draw bias (43% of 6f winners high over six years), and Daniel Tudhope’s strong recent book outweigh the bare 1.8L reversal—but only narrowly. Lord Roxby’s course-and-distance win a fortnight ago, lighter weight, and proven suitability count heavily; Alex Jary’s inexperience (0-0 in fourteen days) is a negative, yet he already navigated draw 6 here successfully. **Fast Track Harry** and draw-favoured **Kodiac Thriller** are next tier (~7–8%) without convincing Ripon/C&D proof at this class; the rest are largely trip, draw, or form mismatches in a deep handicap.

The biggest risk to Dark Cloud Rising as the marginal top line is that Lord Roxby has already solved this exact puzzle—same track, trip, and going—and markets shortening the rematch favourite pair (7.0 / 7.2) leave little margin for error at my calibrated rates (claims in the 0.25–0.40 band have under-hit at 23%). Without a clear overlay and with three Easterby runners and two Walford runners…

pace map with Skirt Around marked pMusical Accord official rating unknownBlue Tulip turf-on-good proof beyond AW win
Clocker is the most reliable win candidate on the evidence available. He is the only runner with a recent twelve-furlong pointer — a close second at Leicester on good ground — plus a good-ground win at Hamilton and a 1-2 going record today; draw two sits in Ripon’s strongest twelve-furlong band (~40% of winners), Edward Bethell and Oisin Orr are both ranking well on the card, and 9-4 on a 65 mark looks fairly treated in a weak Class 5. Talitha Rouge is next best on the 68 rating, low draw, and Tudhope’s recent book, but David O’Meara is 0-0 in fourteen days, she is stepping up in trip off three runs, and her Sandown sixth reads more like a near-miss place profile than a ready winner.

The main danger is that this is still a very inexperienced handicap where the market’s 1.5 on Clocker reflects the obvious form line rather than dominance — Blue Tulip’s AW twelve-furlong win and Talitha’s superior handicap mark mean a true win chance around 0.32, not a short-priced certainty.

CursorRiddikulus · 14%
Risk Draw 14 is a material downgrade from draw 3 when he won here 17 days ago in a deep 15-runner handicap.
unclear pace map with three Tim Easterby runnersMarlena's Prince debut ability unknownwhether Good ground rides truly uniform after recent rain
Riddikulus is the most grounded win angle on form and suitability, not price. He won this exact Ripon 10f Good Class 6 handicap on 27 July, holds strong course-and-distance credentials (CD 1-2, C 2-3), and arrives off a close fourth at Catterick rather than a collapse — the profile of a horse still handling its mark at OR50. Ripon’s 10f draw split is fairly flat (low 30%, mid 38%, high 32%), so a wide berth is not fatal for a local specialist who already knows the bends and run-in.

The main reservation is the race shape, not ability. Sunny Orange looks the clearest challenger on recent 10f form — second at Pontefract and third at Beverley, both beaten a neck or less, from draw 5 in the statistically friendliest mid band — with Magic Runner (D 2-16, draw 3) and Tiberio Force (CD 1-5, draw 1) live on map and track knowledge despite poor recent figures. None of the 1.1 quotes mean anything here; this is an open Class 6 with no dominant runner, which is why the win probability stays modest at 0.14 despite Riddikulus being the best single ticket.

Risk Three wins on the bounce often attract a tough mark and the yard runs cold lately (2-33).
pace map and early speedmeaning of the 'p' flag on Poet's Dawnfinal market prices (all shown at 1.1)
Poet's Dawn is the most convincing winner profile on trip and ground: three straight wins at 10f on good or good to firm, including Ripon and Nottingham, with a strong 5-15 distance record overall. The 72 OR and 9-5 look workable rather than greedy after those wins, and Tim Easterby is the best-ranked trainer on the card. Draw bias here is flat, so stall four is neutral. I would not treat the lowest rating as weakness when recent evidence at this trip is this strong.

The main challenge is sustainability after a hat-trick — yards in patchy form and a 3lb claim jockey add variance — while Moonjid is the logical second: proven 10f, drops from Class 3 to Class 5 off a close fifth at Pontefract in a small field, and suits good to firm. Amidst The Chaos is in good heart and has course form plus draw 2, but has no runs at 10f (D 0-0), which caps him below the top two. Canvas has Doncaster credentials (2-4) and top weight, but two poor runs in the last month make him hard to trust as favourite material. Qitaal’s draw-one slot is offset by 0-7 on good going; Echalar and the 94-day-off Project Geofin look out of the picture on today’s terms.

true market prices (all shown 1.1)official ratings/handicap marksworkouts since last run
Cercis is the most informative form line in a thin race: second-start 4th at Nottingham on good to firm, beaten only half a length in a Class 4 turf contest where she had traffic/stewards’ involvement — that reads as competitive ability on today’s surface. She is also the most recently race-fit (25 days) with going suitability the others lack; Hope And Joy and One Of The Boys have shown little on AW, while Wuood’s Newcastle second is respectable but on a different surface and trip after a long break.

The biggest risk is projection: her best run was six furlongs with top weight here, and Wuood brings Richard Hannon/Sean Levey form plus the high draw (39% of Doncaster 7f winners), so fitness and class from the yard could overturn a marginal form edge. I would not treat any runner as a strong banker — true win chance stays near one-in-three at best, which is why the model’s no-bet stance is reasonable even with Cercis slightly preferred.

Thapa VC is the most race-specific profile: back-to-back 7f wins on good ground including Doncaster 18 days ago (CD 1-4), then a confirming Yarmouth success, in the high-draw third that has produced 39% of 7f winners here. The 7lb claim offsets much of the OR gap in a deep Class 5, and he arrives with clear course-and-distance suitability that Imperial Guard and the higher-rated types lack.

The main danger is Imperial Guard, whose 688111 line and 2-5 at seven furlongs mark him as the form horse of the field from a high draw, regardless of Dods’s quiet T14. If Thapa VC is overplayed on the double, Guard’s sustained winning habit at the trip could see him through; locally, Age Of Baroque’s June Doncaster 7f GF second and War Howl’s CD record are the sneaky each-way threats if the pace collapses or the favourite flops.

CursorCeltic Chariot · 24%
Risk Top weight (9-10) against three rivals 3–7lb lighter on favourable low draws in a tight Class 5.
pace map / Vega's Virtue rolesectional profile beyond headline speedfirmness within Good To Firm
Celtic Chariot is the most reliable winner candidate, not because of any market price, but because he has already won over this exact course and distance on Good To Firm and arrives on a clear upward curve with back-to-back wins at Yarmouth and Doncaster. That is rare proof in a seven-runner handicap. Jack Mitchell is the strongest jockey stat on the card, and the mid draw (stall 5) is only a minor negative in a race where low stalls have a modest edge — it is not enough to overturn proven C&D form.

The main reason his true chance is nearer one-in-four than the model’s 55% is the handicap itself: he carries the heaviest weight in the field while Berlinetta (draw 3, D 1-1, fresh 8f GF win), Lady Hornblower (draw 1, 9-3, unlucky third at Beverley), and Vega’s Virtue (Easterby in form, beaten a neck latest) all come in materially lighter and from the preferred draw half. One strong C&D winner does not dominate a competitive Class 5; several others have plausible winning profiles, so confidence should stay calibrated rather than short-priced certainty.

early pace/mapSound Gloria's ability to see out 14.5f on debut at tripwhether ground stays good-to-firm
Character Testing gets the nod mainly on suitability and draw: stall 5 sits in the strongest Doncaster 14f zone (mid 44%), his latest run was a clear second on good to firm over 12f, and the Cartmel second over 17f confirms he stays this far better than most rivals. Mark Walford/Jack Garritty are cold on the card, but that is secondary to trip, going, and draw alignment in a weak Class 6.

The model’s Sound Gloria angle overrates a four-run filly whose only win came at 12f — a sharp step down from today’s 14.5f — and a low draw (24% win share) is a further headwind. Is She Now is the main danger: proven over 16f at Newcastle and two close seconds, though 1–26 strike rate and a high draw leave her vulnerable if Character Testing finally converts a placing.

CursorStepdance · 26%

pace map / who leadsin-race tactical role for Slattery pairfull timefigure comparison vs OR compression
Stepdance is the most coherent profile for this specific test: two wins from two over Tramore 12f, two course wins from three, and solid good-ground/distance records, all from draw 10 in a race where high stalls have taken roughly three-fifths of winners over six years. Henry De Bromhead is the strongest trainer on the card by recent strike rate, and the horse is not giving away weight to the main market rivals at the same OR band. That outweighs, narrowly, the flashier recent placings elsewhere in the field—Metamorpheus’s two seconds and Miss Australie’s wide draw are real threats, but neither brings the same proven C&D edge at this trip.

The biggest risk is treating the 2–2 course-and-distance record as bankable when the last three runs tell a different story: pulled up over an longer Tramore trip, beaten less than a length but only tenth of twenty-two at Leopardstown, and well held at Roscommon. At a true win chance around one-in-four—not the fifty percent the model implies—this is a marginal favourite in a messy handicap, not a short-priced certainty; Metamorpheus (draw 8, in-form, well treated on weight) is the most likely upset if Stepdance fails to translate stall and…

CursorMiss Gitana · 20%
Risk Inconsistent 30-start profile could revert to empty runs despite CD and weight edges.
Tramore 16f stall/draw bias detailSpasiba readiness after 587-day layoffpace map and who controls the lead
Miss Gitana is my marginal leader on true chance, not market price. She is a proven course-and-distance winner (CD 1-1), draws well (3 of 9) in a race where draw has mattered in settled lessons, carries the lightest handicap load (OR 62, 8-9 with a 7lb claim), and arrives off a neck-beating third over 15f on Good — form that says she belongs with this company despite big SPs. Filey Bay shares the CD stat but his 19/20 collapse and same-yard tension with the top-weight Dream On Baby weaken him; Delta has the best immediate form but only one 16f run (10th) and a middling draw.

The main danger is Delta: a 0.8L second at Leopardstown on Good off a short price is genuine ability, and J J Slevin’s recent strike adds a connections edge. If he stays the trip better than his 0-1 distance record implies, he beats her; Spasiba is a secondary latent threat if Mullins has him fit after a long absence, but that fitness gap is too large to rank him above the two form/course angles.

CursorNO BET · 20%
Risk Bynx is the logical leader but ~20% true win chance is far below evens/implied 50%.
post-win handicap reassessmentTramore 16f draw/pace mapjockey bookings on several runners
Bynx is the right top line on form: he won this exact Tramore 16f Good test on 07-07 (CD 1-4, course form 2-6), handles the ground (2-10), carries a light 9-12 from OR 48, and has a useful low draw (2). That is a clear edge on suitability — but not a 45% edge in a 14-runner handicap. The prior Tramore run was 8th (beaten 8L), connections are cold (T14 0-2), and repeat winners in big-field handicaps win closer to one time in five than one in two; I rate him ~20%, with Synchronize next at ~14% on the same July card (6/12, beaten only 0.5L) off bottom weight OR 41/9-1, plus Lariat (~9%) who was 2nd here before his PU.

The main reason to pass is price, not profile: the model’s 45% and evens treat the July win as proof at a level the data does not support. Synchronize’s close defeat under a lower mark, God Of Thunder’s Sligo stamina (2nd 18f Good), and Vervain’s fresh Good-ground form all keep this from being a single-horse race; I would need a much bigger price than 1.0 to stake Bynx.

London Is Blue is the most credible 5f player on figures and trip: OR 73 tops this Class 5, with a 2-9 distance record versus Wyle Cop's 0-4 at five furlongs and Stock Market's 0-3. Robert Cowell (1-2) and Edward Greatrex (3-11) are the hottest connections on the card, and a prominent ride from draw 3 in a four-runner field is workable despite Lingfield's high-draw lean (41% high). I don't trust the market to do the work here—Wyle Cop's 1.0 win was context, not proof he repeats at this trip.

Monks Mead looks the most fairly treated runner in an open Class 6. He has twice been beaten only a length or less at Lingfield over this trip/class recently, carries a useful 8-9 from OR 46 against rivals in the high 50s/low 60s, and Luke Morris is the strongest jockey stat on the card. Course-and-distance form (1-9, 1-3 CD) matters more here than a blanket speed figure, and his fresh 11-day profile fits a horse who keeps finding this track.

The main danger is that he keeps finishing third rather than winning, with a slow-start report in the stewards’ notes — in a field where Sansanetti (CD 1-1, 4-9 at 10f, good draw 7 in a high-bias zone) and Sceptic (AW winner, same OR tier, draw 8) both have clearer win claims on ratings and surface. I do not share the model’s 52% on Sansanetti at 1.0; recent 644 form, no win in six runs, and a hung/interference run at Windsor cap his true chance nearer low-20s than evens.

This is a genuinely open Class 4 staying handicap, not a race to trust any 1.1 placeholder prices. Way Maker gets the nod on the best combination of proven trip, Good-ground form, and direct course-and-distance relevance: he was third here on 5 July over 20f on Good ground, beaten only 3L when sent off favourite, and his prior Southwell second over 20f confirms he stays. OR 107 puts him among the logical top weights, James Bowen is a solid NH rider, and 41 days since that Rasen run is a workable gap. Brosna Town finished ahead of him that day and arrives fitter off 14 days, but his Galway flop since then and lower OR 80 suggest that Rasen run may have been his ceiling rather than a repeatable profile; he is the main danger, not the most trustworthy winner.

The biggest hole in the Way Maker case is completion: the Uttoxeter unseat between two otherwise respectable staying efforts is exactly the sort of jumping lapse that hurts over 20.5f, and Brosna Town has already beaten him here. Park Hall is the Skelton/Skeleton wildcard — top yard, unbeaten, but only one run at 17f — while Jentobello’s ratings and 1-1 course record look appealing on paper but 298 days off makes him a fitness…

CursorLoriko · 46%
Risk His latest was over 20f at this track — shortening to 16.5f may suit Eternal Angel's sharper profile better.
Eternal Angel has no course form (0-0 C/CD)Mayo OR unrated — ability ceiling unclearBoth leading yards/jockeys are 0-0 in last 14 days
Loriko is the logical winner on merit: top OR (121), the strongest NH connections on the card (Dan Skelton / Harry Skelton), clean jumping in recent form, a win at Uttoxeter over ~16f in this class, and a neck-beating second at Market Rasen four weeks ago. Eternal Angel matches him on recent C4 hurdle wins and carries only 1lb less on the ratings, but Loriko's course-and-trip composite is stronger and the Skelton operation's yard/jockey statistics materially outweigh Tom Lacey/Jonathan Burke here.

The biggest risk is that Loriko's Rasen run was over 20f on good ground; Eternal Angel looks more purpose-built for this exact trip (2-5 at distance vs Loriko's 1-4) and arrives off a respectable Class 3 third at Cartmel, so he is a very live second and could flip the result if Loriko finds 16.5f too sharp. Destination Unkown (two pull-ups in form, OR 46) and Mayo (0-4, 70 days off, no wins) are fringe win chances only — together perhaps 12–14% — and should not drive the market narrative despite the thin four-runner field.

Clean Getaway is the most convincing profile for a 17f Good chase here without leaning on the false 1.1 market: he is a proven Market Rasen horse (2-4 course-and-distance, 2-5 at the track), with strong going and trip records (6-24 Good, 6-21 at distance), no recent P/F/U in his form, and he arrives fit off a narrow 1.2L third at Cartmel. At OR 88 and 10-8 he looks the best-treated runner in a field where several higher-rated types are carrying weight and running poorly.

The main challenge is that Belle Le Grand and My Friend Sean still have superior ratings and Dan Skelton/Harry Skelton are the standout connections on the card — but Belle’s 7-5-6 recent line and My Friend Sean’s 5-6-5 pattern, both well beaten, do not justify anything like a 48% win chance. Dog Fox is the clearest danger after winning over the same 17f Good Class 4 chase template at Cartmel, but the unseat and pull-up in his recent six make him a riskier second choice than Clean Getaway’s reliable completion record.

Ballintubber Boy is the most coherent profile for a 23f good-ground Rasen handicap: he completes consistently (no recent P/F/U), is 6-15 on good and 1-2 at the course, and his latest run was fourth over 23f on good at Worcester — essentially today's test — beaten a manageable 4.2L. At OR 122 he is only 1lb below the top weight, so he looks fairly treated rather than flattered by a soft mark, and he has the experience (25 runs) this competitive six-runner handicap needs.

The main doubt is that nothing here screams a standout winner — Ernest Gray is burdened with top weight off a 14L defeat, Kiwi de Cotte is only three runs with a PU on his record and a 21L flop since his Rasen win, Belvedere Blast is a course regular but ninth here over 20f last time, and Parikarma relies on a 7lb claim with a 10L second in a five-runner race. Lowlands is the main danger on pure recent form (won at Perth, close second at Cartmel), but with no course or distance form he is the bigger unknown on this quirky track; I have him a touch behind on balance, which is why the model's no-bet stance is understandable even though I marginally prefer Ballintubber Boy.

Ashdown Forest is the most coherent profile: a fresh Good-ground hurdle winner (Uttoxeter, 22 days), Dan Skelton’s yard ranked #1 nationally over six months, and Harry Skelton in the saddle. At OR 89 and 11-2 he avoids the 12st burden on No More Bolero and Fine Point, jumping has been reliable (no P/F/U in recent form), and Good suits him (1-2). No More Bolero is the main danger on back-to-back wins and a 1-1 course record, but both victories were over 16f and top weight in a deep Class 5 handicap is a meaningful drag; Fine Point fits the trip (Hexham 20f third) yet 70 days off raises fitness doubt.
